Illegal vehicle possession: Johnston fined Rs. 130,000, handed suspended sentence

cards.what_happened: Former Minister Johnston Fernando was fined a total of Rs. 130,000 and given a six-month suspended prison sentence by the Colombo Fort Magistrate's Court today (25) for illegally possessing a vehicle.
details: Former Minister Johnston Fernando appeared at the Colombo Fort Magistrate's Court today (25) in a case about the illegal possession of a vehicle. The court found him guilty and imposed a total fine of Rs. 130,000 along with a six-month suspended prison sentence.

On the first charge, he was fined Rs. 5,000, with a three-month prison sentence if he does not pay. On the second charge, Fernando was fined Rs. 100,000 and sentenced to six months of simple imprisonment, suspended for five years.
On the third charge, the court fined him Rs. 25,000, with a three-month sentence of simple imprisonment in default of payment. The verdict and all penalties were reported by Newswire.
key_facts: Former Minister Johnston Fernando fined Rs. 130,000 total by the court.
Colombo Fort Magistrate's Court gave a six-month suspended sentence today (25).
The case involved the illegal possession of a vehicle.
First charge: Rs. 5,000 fine, three months in prison if unpaid.
Second charge: Rs. 100,000 fine, six months suspended for five years.
Third charge: Rs. 25,000 fine, three months in prison if unpaid.
cards.blurb: Former Minister Johnston Fernando fined Rs. 130,000 and given a suspended sentence for illegal vehicle possession.
cards.spoken: Hello and welcome to the news. A former minister named Johnston Fernando has been sentenced by the Colombo Fort Magistrate's Court. The case was about the illegal possession of a vehicle, and the verdict came out today (25). The court fined him a total of Rs. 130,000 and gave him a six month suspended prison sentence. For the first charge, he must pay Rs. 5,000 or spend three months in prison. For the second charge, he was fined Rs. 100,000 and sentenced to six months of simple imprisonment, suspended for five years. For the third charge, the fine is Rs. 25,000, with three months of simple imprisonment if he does not pay. This report is from Newswire.
